messages:
Jess: FYI a customer pinged about a missing day in the daily usage chart — their org shows 0 for 2026-03-14 in the console, but the raw CSV export contains ~12k tokens for that day. Org tz is Europe/Berlin. Can someone look?

Maria: Which export did they run (UI download vs API)? Screenshot? org id?

Jess: They used the UI CSV (Console -> Billing -> Export) and attached CSV. Org ID: org_03X. Screenshot: "chart shows flatline for Mar 14, export rows attached". Quick excerpt from the CSV they pasted: 
```
org_id,usage_ts,model,tokens
org_03X,2026-03-14T23:45:12+01:00,gpt-lite,4321
org_03X,2026-03-15T00:05:01+01:00,gpt-lite,7890
```
They expect both rows to be counted for Mar 14 in the console (their business day is 03:00-02:59 local), but Console shows Mar 14 total = 0, Mar 15 = full count.

jon_eng: Copying in eng — this smells like a day-boundary normalization bug between the charting service and export codepaths. Charting may be using UTC floor while export respects org tz + custom day start. Can you confirm the org-level "day_start_hour" setting?

Jess: They say they didn't change day_start_hour (default). Their org timezone is Europe/Berlin (CET/CEST) and I suspect DST transition was last week. They did not set a custom day start.

lia_prod: metrics_bot, can you fetch the aggregation config for org_03X and the last 7 days' ingestion latencies?

metrics_bot: Retrieved config for org_03X: timezone=Europe/Berlin, day_start=00:00 (org-local), retention=90d. Ingestion latencies: median=12s, 99p=3m12s, spike on 2026-03-14 at 02:58 -> 03:10 UTC (ingestion lag ~12m).

jon_eng: That ingestion spike coincides with when events crossed DST boundary. If the charting job used a UTC-based bucketing and then translated labels, late-arriving rows with local timestamps near midnight could have been assigned to the wrong bucket at render time. Need to verify aggregation window code: are we doing floor(utc_ts, 1d) and then shifting label by tz vs grouping by local date?

lia_prod: Repro plan: 1) Run local script to simulate events at 2026-03-14T23:50:00+01:00 and 2026-03-15T00:05:00+01:00, push through ingestion, then call UI chart query for date=2026-03-14 with org tz=Europe/Berlin. 2) Export CSV from UI for the same date range and compare sums.

jon_eng: Also check exporter: /api/v1/usage/export currently accepts ?start_date & ?end_date and an optional tz param. I think UI export adds tz param but chart query does not. If chart query always groups by UTC day boundaries while exporter applies tz folding, you'll see mismatches.

Jess: Customer wants workaround now — suggested they download full export and run a local group-by with their tz. They asked if we can offer an interim console patch (e.g., respect org tz in charts) — can we toggle that?

jon_eng: Short-term workaround: we can expose a query param in the chart API to force tz-aware grouping, but that's a backend change + minor front-end wiring. I'll add a feature flag and a quick fix to treat chart grouping like exporter.

lia_prod: I pushed a small probe to prod metrics service to log the grouping codepath for org_03X for requests touching 2026-03-14. Logs: 
```
[metrics] request=chart_query org=org_03X date=2026-03-14 grouping_bucket=utc_day
[metrics] export_request org=org_03X date=2026-03-14 tz=Europe/Berlin grouping_bucket=local_day
```
Shows mismatch.

jon_eng: Ok confirmed. Root cause: charting pipeline uses bucket = floor(utc_ts) then converts label => local date; exporter uses bucket = floor(local_ts). When ingestion lag pushes events across DST boundary, the two yield different counts. Fix: switch charting grouping to use floor(local_ts, 1d) using org tz. I'll draft a patch.

maria_support: Thanks. Can we create an incident/ticket so support can keep the customer updated?

jon_eng: Created INC-1234, assigned to eng-runtime, label priority=high, ETA for patch to staging today EOD, canary tomorrow, prod roll early next week.

Jess: Customer updated — they want a note when their Mar 14 numbers are reconciled in console. I'll let them know we opened INC-1234 and provide the CSV workaround.

lia_prod: For transparency, adding suggested regression test: ingest synthetic events around local midnight both before and after DST switch and assert chart vs export parity. Also add a note in release notes about timezone handling for charts.

jon_eng: Patch submitted: change grouping to use tz-aware bucketing util, added unit tests, and a migration that re-aggregates last 7 days for orgs with non-UTC tz if ingestion lag > 10s. Will follow up with deployment pr.

maria_support: :thumbsup: please cc me on the canary.

metrics_bot: Canary deploy started for change-set arc-2026-03-tzfix on canary host set alpha. Monitoring target: chart discrepancy rate for orgs with tz != UTC.

jon_eng: Noted a pre-check: when re-aggregating historical days we must avoid double counting if exporter rows were already ingested under the previous aggregation scheme. I'll add idempotency via aggregation version stamp.

Jess: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and move thread to follow-up.

maria_support: Closing loop: customer replied "thanks — appreciate the quick response". Marking as escalated -> eng.

jon_eng: Final: INC-1234 -> status=in-progress, next update tomorrow after canary.
